readings.title: The First Journey to Egypt
readings.subtitle: Joseph Tests His Brothers
readings.text: [Genesis 42:1] And when Ya‛aqoḇ saw that there was grain in Mitsrayim, Ya‛aqoḇ said to his sons, “Why do you look at each other?” [2] And he said, “See, I have heard that there is grain in Mitsrayim. Go down to that place and buy for us there, and let us live and not die.” [3] And Yosěph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain in Mitsrayim. [4] But Ya‛aqoḇ did not send <dn>את</dn> Yosěph’s brother Binyamin with <dn>את</dn> his brothers, for he said, “Lest some harm come to him.” [5] And the sons of Yisra’ěl went to buy grain among those who journeyed, for the scarcity of food was in the land of Kena‛an. [6] And Yosěph was the governor over the land, he was the one who sold to all the people of the land. And Yosěph’s brothers came and bowed down before him with their faces to the earth. [7] And Yosěph saw <dn>את</dn> his brothers and recognised them, but he acted as a stranger to them and spoke to them harshly, and said to them, “Where do you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Kena‛an to buy food.” [8] So Yosěph recognised <dn>את</dn> his brothers, but they did not recognise him. [9] And Yosěph remembered <dn>את</dn> the dreams which he had dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see <dn>את</dn> the nakedness of the land!” [10] And they said to him, “No, my master, but your servants have come to buy food. [11] “We are all one man’s sons, we are trustworthy, your servants are not spies.” [12] But he said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land.” [13] And they said, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Kena‛an. And see, the youngest is with <dn>את</dn> our father today, and one is no more.” [14] And Yosěph said to them, “It is as I spoke to you, saying, ‘You are spies!’ [15] “By this you shall be proven: By the life of Pharaoh, you do not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here. [16] “Send one of you, and let him bring <dn>את</dn> your brother, while you are kept in prison. So let your words be proven to see whether there is any truth in you, or else, by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies!” [17] And he put <dn>את</dn> them all together in prison for three days. [18] Now Yosěph said to them the third day, “Do this and live, for I fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>: [19] “If you are trustworthy, let one of your brothers be confined to your prison house, and you, go, bring grain for the scarcity of food of your houses. [20] “And bring <dn>את</dn> your youngest brother to me, and let your words be confirmed, and you do not die.” And so they did. [21] And they said to each other, “Truly, we are guilty concerning our brother, for we saw the distress of his life when he pleaded with us, yet we did not listen, that is why this distress has come upon us.” [22] And Re’uḇěn answered <dn>את</dn> them, saying, “Did I not speak to you, saying, ‘Do not sin against the boy,’ and you would not listen? And see, his blood is now required of us.” [23] And they did not know that Yosěph understood them, for he spoke to them through an interpreter. [24] And he turned himself away from them and wept, but came back to them and spoke to them. And he took <dn>את</dn> Shim‛on from them and bound <dn>את</dn> him before their eyes. [25] And Yosěph commanded and they filled <dn>את</dn> their sacks with grain, also to put back every man’s silver to his sack, and to give them food for the journey. And thus it was done for them. [26] So they loaded their donkeys with the grain and went from there. [27] And as one of them opened <dn>את</dn> his sack to give his donkey fodder at the lodging place, he saw <dn>את</dn> his silver, for there it was in the mouth of his sack! [28] And he said to his brothers, “My silver has been returned, and there it is, in my sack!” And their hearts sank and they were afraid, saying to each other, “What is this that <dn>Elohim</dn> has done to us?” [29] So they came to Ya‛aqoḇ their father in the land of Kena‛an and reported to him <dn>את</dn> all that befell them, saying, [30] “The man, the master of the land, spoke to us harshly, and took <dn>את</dn> us for spies of <dn>את</dn> the land. [31] “But we said to him, ‘We are trustworthy, we are not spies. [32] We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is today with <dn>את</dn> our father in the land of Kena‛an.’ [33] “And the man, the master of the land, said to us, ‘By this I know that you are trustworthy: Leave one of your brothers here with <dn>את</dn> me, and take <dn>את</dn> food for the scarcity of food of your households, and go. [34] And bring <dn>את</dn> your youngest brother to me, then I know that you are not spies, but that you are trustworthy – I give <dn>את</dn> your brother to you, and you move about in the land.’ ” [35] And it came to be as they emptied their sacks, that look, the bundle of each man’s silver was in his sack! And when they and their father saw <dn>את</dn> the bundles of silver, they were afraid. [36] And Ya‛aqoḇ their father said to them, “You have bereaved <dn>את</dn> me – Yosěph is no more, and Shim‛on is no more, and you would take <dn>את</dn> Binyamin! All this is against me.” [37] So Re’uḇěn spoke to his father, saying, “Take the lives of <dn>את</dn> my two sons if I do not bring him back to you. Put <dn>את</dn> him in my hands, and I myself bring him back to you.” [38] But he said, “My son is not going down with you, for his brother is dead, and he is left alone. If any harm should come to him along the way in which you go, then you would bring down <dn>את</dn> my grey hair with sorrow to She’ol.”

readings.title: The Second Journey
readings.subtitle: Benjamin Goes to Egypt
readings.text: [Genesis 43:1] But the scarcity of food was severe in the land. [2] And it came to be, when they had eaten up <dn>את</dn> the grain which they had brought from Mitsrayim, that their father said to them, “Go back, buy us a little food.” [3] But Yehuḏah spoke to him, saying, “The man vehemently warned us, saying, ‘You do not see my face unless your brother is with <dn>את</dn> you.’ ” [4] “If you let <dn>את</dn> our brother go with <dn>את</dn> us, we go down and buy you food. [5] “But if you do not let him go, we do not go down, because the man said to us, ‘You do not see my face unless your brother is with <dn>את</dn> you.’ ” [6] And Yisra’ěl said, “Why did you do evil to me to inform the man that you still had another brother?” [7] And they said, “The man kept asking about us and our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ And we informed him according to these words. How could we know that he would say, ‘Bring <dn>את</dn> your brother down’?” [8] And Yehuḏah said to Yisra’ěl his father, “Send the boy with <dn>את</dn> me, and let us arise and go, and live and not die, both we and you and also our little ones. [9] “I myself shall stand guaranty for him – from my hand you are to require him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever. [10] “For if we had not delayed, truly by now we could have returned this second time.” [11] And their father Yisra’ěl said to them, “If so, then do this: Take some of the best fruit of the land in your vessels and bring a present down for the man, a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts and almonds. [12] “And take double silver in your hand, and take back in your hand <dn>את</dn> the silver that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. It could have been a mistake. [13] “And take <dn>את</dn> your brother, and arise, go back to the man. [14] “And <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai give to you compassion before the man, so that he shall release <dn>את</dn> your other brother and <dn>את</dn> Binyamin. And I, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved!” [15] And the men took <dn>את</dn> that present and <dn>את</dn> Binyamin, and they took double the amount of silver in their hand, and arose and went down to Mitsrayim, and stood before Yosěph. [16] And Yosěph saw <dn>את</dn> Binyamin with <dn>את</dn> them, and said to the one over his house, “Bring <dn>את</dn> the men home, and make a great slaughter, and prepare, for these men are to eat with <dn>את</dn> me at noon.” [17] And the man did as Yosěph said, and the man brought <dn>את</dn> the men into Yosěph’s house. [18] And the men were afraid because they were brought into Yosěph’s house. And they said, “It is because of the silver, which was put back into our sacks the first time, that we are brought in, to throw himself upon us and fall upon us, to take <dn>את</dn> us as slaves, <dn>את</dn> our donkeys too.” [19] So they came near to the man over the house of Yosěph, and spoke to him at the door of the house, [20] and said, “O my master, we indeed came down the first time to buy food, [21] but it came to be, when we came to the lodging place, that we opened <dn>את</dn> our sacks and saw each man’s silver in the mouth of his sack, our silver in its weight. And we have brought <dn>את</dn> it back in our hand. [22] “And we have brought down other silver in our hands to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.” [23] But he said, “Peace be with you, do not be afraid. Your <dn>Elohim</dn> and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father has given you treasure in your sacks – your silver had come to me!” And he brought <dn>את</dn> Shim‛on out to them. [24] And the man brought <dn>את</dn> the men into Yosěph’s house and gave them water, and they washed their feet. And he gave their donkeys fodder. [25] And they made <dn>את</dn> the present ready for Yosěph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they were to eat there. [26] And when Yosěph came home, they brought him <dn>את</dn> the present which was in their hand, into the house, and bowed down before him to the earth. [27] And he asked them about their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?” [28] And they said, “Your servant our father is in good health, he is still alive.” And they bowed their heads down and did obeisance. [29] And he lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> his brother Binyamin, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your younger brother of whom you spoke to me?” And he said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> show favour to you, my son.” [30] And Yosěph hurried, for his emotions were deeply moved towards his brother, and he looked for a place to weep, and went into his room and wept there. [31] Then he washed his face and came out, and controlled himself, and said, “Serve the food.” [32] And they set him a place by himself, and them by themselves, and the Mitsrites who ate with <dn>את</dn> him by themselves, for the Mitsrites could not eat food with <dn>את</dn> the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Mitsrites. [33] And they sat before him, the first-born according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at each other in astonishment. [34] And he took portions to them from before him, but Binyamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. And they feasted and they drank with him.

readings.title: The Silver Cup
readings.subtitle: Judah's Plea
readings.text: [Genesis 44:1] And he commanded <dn>את</dn> the one over his house, saying, “Fill <dn>את</dn> the men’s sacks with food, as they are able to bear, and put each man’s silver in the mouth of his sack. [2] “And put <dn>את</dn> my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and <dn>את</dn> the silver for his grain.” And he did according to the word of Yosěph which he spoke. [3] As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys. [4] And when they had gone out of <dn>את</dn> the city, not having gone far, Yosěph said to the one over his house, “Rise up, follow the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good? [5] Is this not the one from which my master drinks, and with which he indeed divines? You have done evil in what you have done.’ ” [6] So he overtook them and spoke <dn>את</dn> these words to them. [7] And they said to him, “Why does my master say these words? Far be it from us that your servants should do according to this word. [8] “See, we brought back to you from the land of Kena‛an the silver which we found in the mouth of our sacks. How then should we steal silver or gold from your master’s house? [9] “With whomever of your servants it is found – he shall die and we shall become my master’s slaves as well.” [10] And he said, “Now also let it be according to your words: he with whom it is found becomes my slave, and you are innocent.” [11] And they hurried, each man let down <dn>את</dn> his sack to the ground, and each opened <dn>את</dn> his sack. [12] And he searched, with the oldest first and with the youngest last, and the cup was found in Binyamin’s sack. [13] And they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey and went back to the city. [14] And Yehuḏah and his brothers came to Yosěph’s house, and he was still there. And they fell before him on the ground. [15] And Yosěph said to them, “What deed is this you have done? Did you not know that a man like me indeed divines?” [16] And Yehuḏah said, “What do we say to my master? What do we speak? Or how do we clear ourselves? <dn>Elohim</dn> has found out <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of your servants. See, we are my master’s slaves, both we and he also with whom the cup was found.” [17] But he said, “Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose hand the cup was found, he becomes my slave. And you, go up in peace to your father.” [18] And Yehuḏah came near to him and said, “O my master, please let your servant speak a word in my master’s hearing, and do not let your displeasure burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh. [19] “My master asked <dn>את</dn> his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’ [20] “And we said to my master, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a young child of his old age, and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’ [21] “And you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, and let me set my eyes on him.’ [22] “And we said to my master, ‘The boy is not able to leave <dn>את</dn> his father, for if he leaves <dn>את</dn> his father, his father shall die.’ [23] “But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with <dn>את</dn> you, you do not see my face again.’ [24] “And it came to be, when we went up to your servant my father, that we told him <dn>את</dn> the words of my master. [25] “And our father said, ‘Go back and buy us a little food.’ [26] “But we said, ‘We are not able to go down. If our youngest brother is with <dn>את</dn> us, then we shall go down, for we are not able to see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with <dn>את</dn> us.’ [27] “Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons, [28] and the one went out from me, and I said, “Truly, he is torn, torn to pieces!” And I have not seen him since. [29] And if you take <dn>את</dn> this one from me too, and harm comes to him, you shall bring down <dn>את</dn> my grey hair with evil to She’ol.’ [30] “And now, if I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with <dn>את</dn> us – since his own life is bound up in his life – [31] then it shall be, when he sees that the boy is not with us, that he shall die. So your servants shall bring down <dn>את</dn> the grey hair of your servant our father with evil to She’ol. [32] “For your servant went guaranty for <dn>את</dn> the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall be a sinner before my father forever.’ [33] “And now, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a slave to my master, and let the boy go up with his brothers. [34] “For how do I go up to my father if the boy is not with <dn>את</dn> me, lest I see the evil that would come upon my father?”

readings.title: The Revelation
readings.subtitle: Joseph Makes Himself Known
readings.text: [Genesis 45:1] And Yosěph was unable to restrain himself before all those who stood by him, and he called out, “Have everyone go out from me!” So no one stood with <dn>את</dn> him while Yosěph made himself known to his brothers. [2] And he wept aloud, and the Mitsrites and the house of Pharaoh heard it. [3] And Yosěph said to his brothers, “I am Yosěph, is my father still alive?” But his brothers were unable to answer <dn>את</dn> him, for they trembled before him. [4] Then Yosěph said to his brothers, “Please come near to me.” And when they came near, he said, “I am Yosěph your brother, whom you sold into Mitsrayim. [5] “And now, do not be grieved nor displeased with yourselves because you sold <dn>את</dn> me here, for <dn>Elohim</dn> sent me before you to preserve life. [6] “For two years now the scarcity of food has been in the land, and there are still five years in which there is neither ploughing nor harvesting. [7] “And <dn>Elohim</dn> sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to give life to you by a great escape. [8] “So then, you did not send <dn>את</dn> me here, but <dn>Elohim</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> has set me for a father to Pharaoh, and master of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Mitsrayim. [9] “Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Yosěph, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has made me master of all Mitsrayim. Come down to me, do not delay. [10] “And you shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and be near to me, you and your children, your children’s children, your flocks and your herds, and all that you have. [11] “And I shall provide for <dn>את</dn> you there, lest you and your household, and all that you have, come to poverty, because five years of scarcity of food are still to come.” ’ [12] “And look, your eyes and the eyes of my brother Binyamin see that it is my mouth that speaks to you. [13] “And you shall inform my father of <dn>את</dn> all my esteem in Mitsrayim, and of <dn>את</dn> all that you have seen. And you shall hurry and bring <dn>את</dn> my father down here.” [14] And he fell on his brother Binyamin’s neck and wept, and Binyamin wept on his neck. [15] And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and after that his brothers spoke with <dn>את</dn> him. [16] And the report of it was heard by the house of Pharaoh, saying, “The brothers of Yosěph have come.” And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants. [17] And Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: Load <dn>את</dn> your beasts and go, enter the land of Kena‛an, [18] and take <dn>את</dn> your father and <dn>את</dn> your households and come to me, and I give you <dn>את</dn> the best of the land of Mitsrayim, and you eat <dn>את</dn> the fat of the land. [19] And you, you have been commanded, do this: Take wagons out of the land of Mitsrayim for your little ones and your wives. And you shall bring <dn>את</dn> your father, and come. [20] And do not be concerned about your goods, for the best of all the land of Mitsrayim is yours.’ ” [21] And the sons of Yisra’ěl did so. And Yosěph gave them wagons, according to the mouth of Pharaoh, and he gave them food for the journey. [22] He gave to all of them, to each man, changes of garments, but to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments. [23] And he sent to his father this: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Mitsrayim, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, and bread, and food for his father for the journey. [24] So he sent <dn>את</dn> his brothers away, and they left. And he said to them, “Do not quarrel along the way.” [25] And they went up out of Mitsrayim, and came to the land of Kena‛an to Ya‛aqoḇ their father. [26] And they told him, saying, “Yosěph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Mitsrayim.” And Ya‛aqoḇ’s heart ceased, for he did not believe them. [27] But when they spoke to him <dn>את</dn> all the words which Yosěph had spoken to them, and when he saw <dn>את</dn> the wagons which Yosěph had sent to transport <dn>את</dn> him, the spirit of Ya‛aqoḇ their father revived. [28] And Yisra’ěl said, “Enough! My son Yosěph is still alive. Let me go and see him before I die.”
